author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Reduce background-app interference during PS2 emulation tests
summary: Identify periodic downloads, media capture, overlays, synchronization, and notification bursts by correlating hitch timestamps with Android activity, then remove one suspect at a time without disabling essential services blindly.
heroAlt: PCSX2 game list used as a clean idle baseline before starting a controlled performance route

blocks.text: Correlate each hitch with activity outside the emulator

Random pauses may come from cloud photo uploads, app updates, messaging bursts, screen recorders, floating overlays, antivirus scanning, or storage indexing. Closing every process once can hide the culprit without proving it. Start with a normal route and note exact hitch times, then repeat after changing one background workload class. Preserve accessibility, security, and communication features unless the user deliberately chooses a short test window.
Do not force-stop system services, device-management software, accessibility tools, or security components you do not understand. A benchmark is not worth breaking normal device behavior.

items: A route that is smooth enough to make unexpected hitches visible.
Screen recording or a written timestamp method used consistently.
A list of active downloads, synchronization, overlays, and capture tools.
Stable network conditions or a documented offline comparison.
Unchanged emulator profile, temperature, and battery policy.

blocks.text: Remove one workload class per pass

items: 1. Run the normal route and mark every unexpected hitch and notification.
2. Check Android's recent battery, network, and app activity for events near those times.
3. Pause only large downloads and store updates, then repeat the route.
4. Restore them and test cloud synchronization separately.
5. Test screen recording, performance overlays, and floating windows as their own class.
6. Use Do Not Disturb for one pass while preserving alarms and required contacts.
7. Repeat the strongest candidate change to confirm the effect.
8. Re-enable normal services and keep only a narrow, documented gaming exception if needed.

blocks.text: One-variable passes prevent a clean result from being attributed to the wrong app. Timestamp correlation strengthens the case when an external task begins at the same moment as a frame-time spike. Network isolation can help, but it must be compared separately because some games or services react to connectivity changes.
Call an app or service responsible only after its removal and restoration produce repeatable opposite results.

items: Hitches have timestamps rather than vague impressions.
Only one background workload class changes per pass.
The route and device state remain matched.
Restoring the suspect tends to restore the symptom.
Essential services are returned to their normal state.
A shader cache warms during the clean pass: repeat with matched cache state.
The device cools while apps are being changed: normalize temperature.
A random encounter changes workload: select a deterministic route.
The hitch persists offline and with services paused: continue with storage or emulator diagnosis.

blocks.text: Resume updates and synchronization, restore notification and accessibility settings, close temporary profilers, and remove any broad battery exemptions. Retain only a narrowly scoped change whose benefit was confirmed and whose side effects are acceptable.
Android may defer rather than eliminate work

Pausing an app can move its job to the next test instead of removing it. Allow the device to settle before each pass and verify that pending downloads or indexing are not released all at once when conditions change.
